title: One Bridge, Two Queues
briefing: Smoke from an industrial fire is approaching a low-lying neighborhood. A single bridge supports both evacuation traffic and incoming suppression vehicles.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The bridge can sustain two light lanes, but heavy engines require alternating access to avoid stressing temporary joints.
private_intelligence.community: Many households cannot drive; a car-based evacuation order would leave the least mobile residents waiting for buses.
private_intelligence.economy: A warehouse on the exit route contains perishable medicine; complete closure would interrupt regional deliveries.
private_intelligence.safety: Wind may change within an hour, so moving everyone immediately is safer than assuming the smoke plume will remain narrow.

choices.title: Open the Full Exit
choices.description: Make both lanes outbound until the threatened district is clear.
choices.consequence: A rapid exit restores confidence and local movement, but delayed suppression increases exposure for crews and remaining facilities.

choices.title: Reserve Responder Access
choices.description: Protect an inbound responder lane and meter outbound traffic.
choices.consequence: Fire crews arrive reliably, but the slower evacuation and freight restrictions leave households anxious and shops short of stock.

choices.title: Run Assisted Convoys
choices.description: Close private traffic briefly and move buses with escorted vehicles.
choices.consequence: Assisted convoys reach residents without cars and reduce exposure, but staging consumes staff and delays bridge work.
